titleStmt.author: Ning Xu
Dongqing Li

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Transition from inflammation to proliferation: a critical step during wound healing

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the boundary between two named phases of wound healing - IN A PARTITION THE SAME SENTENCE CALLS SEQUENTIAL AND OVERLAPPING, whose first boundary is concurrent and whose second phase has two different durations
span.quote: The wound healing process is usually characterized as four sequential but overlapping phases: haemostasis (0–several hours after injury), inflammation (1–3 days), proliferation (4–21 days) and remodelling (21 days–1 year) [ 1 ]. Deregulation of any of these steps results in impaired healing

span.label: what regulates the passage from the inflammatory to the proliferative phase, given that a compromised transition is associated with wounds that do not heal
span.quote: Transition from the inflammatory to the proliferative phase represents a key step during wound healing. The inflammatory phase is essential leading to haemostasis and recruitment of the innate immune system, which defends us against the attack of invading pathogens and help remove dead tissues

span.label: a review of the cellular and molecular mechanisms regulating the inflammation-proliferation transition, proposed as a source of therapeutic targets
span.quote: Compared with the process of initiation and amplification of the inflammatory response, we know much less about how inflammation is resolved during normal wound healing, which is prerequisite for understanding the pathogenesis of persistent inflammation in chronic wounds [ 6 ]. Moreover, the next step, proliferation, is tightly connected with the inflammatory response, and also plays an important role in resolving inflammation.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: This M1–M2 transition is critical for the resolution of inflammation and tipping the balance to tissue repair

span.label: a continuous repair process that the field partitions into four named phases, with the property naming phase two continuing through all four
span.quote: In normal skin wound healing, the inflammation usually lasts for 2–5 days and ceases once the harmful stimuli have been removed; even though the immune responses continue through the whole procedure of wound healing, evolving through progressive states of specific leukocyte involvement and function

span.label: narrative review; no new measurement
span.quote: Wound healing is often described as a drama, with the interplay of a multitude of different cell types, and is precisely directed to serve the ultimate goal: prompt healing [ 1 ]. Although many questions remain, extensive studies in the field have provided a general picture about this fundamental biological process.

span.label: THE PARTITION CONTRADICTS ITSELF IN THE SENTENCE THAT STATES IT: `The wound healing process is usually characterized as FOUR SEQUENTIAL BUT OVERLAPPING PHASES: haemostasis (0-several hours after injury), inflammation (1-3 days), proliferation (4-21 days) and remodelling (21 days-1 year)`. Four names, four numeric ranges that do NOT overlap as printed, and an adjective saying they do
span.quote: The wound healing process is usually characterized as four sequential but overlapping phases: haemostasis (0–several hours after injury), inflammation (1–3 days), proliferation (4–21 days) and remodelling (21 days–1 year) [ 1 ]. Deregulation of any of these steps results in impaired healing

span.label: AND THE FIRST BOUNDARY IS NOT A BOUNDARY: `In the inflammatory phase ... THIS PHASE IS ACTUALLY CONCURRENT WITH HAEMOSTASIS, and described as the early stage of wound healing`. Phase two runs at the same time as phase one, so `sequential` fails at the very first join
span.quote: In the inflammatory phase, involving mainly activation of the innate immune system, neutrophils and monocytes rapidly migrate into the injured skin. This phase is actually concurrent with haemostasis, and described as the early stage of wound healing

span.label: AND THE PROPERTY THAT NAMES THE PHASE NEVER STOPS: `the inflammation usually lasts for 2-5 days and ceases once the harmful stimuli have been removed; EVEN THOUGH THE IMMUNE RESPONSES CONTINUE THROUGH THE WHOLE PROCEDURE OF WOUND HEALING, evolving through progressive states of specific leukocyte involvement`. What ends on day 3 or day 5 is a STAGE-NAME, not the thing it is named after
span.quote: In normal skin wound healing, the inflammation usually lasts for 2–5 days and ceases once the harmful stimuli have been removed; even though the immune responses continue through the whole procedure of wound healing, evolving through progressive states of specific leukocyte involvement and function

span.label: and the cell type that drives the transition crosses every boundary: macrophages `manifest substantial plasticity in their phenotypes and functions, THAT IS, they can READILY SWITCH FROM ONE FUNCTIONAL PHENOTYPE TO ANOTHER ... versatile players to ASSIST AND ORCHESTRATE ALL STAGES of wound healing`
span.quote: Importantly, they manifest substantial plasticity in their phenotypes and functions, that is, they can readily switch from one functional phenotype to another in response to different microenvironment stimuli [ 54 – 56 ]. These properties make macrophages versatile players to assist and orchestrate all stages of wound healing

span.label: THE SAME PAPER GIVES THE INFLAMMATION PHASE TWO DIFFERENT DURATIONS. The partition says `inflammation (1-3 DAYS)`; the body says `In normal skin wound healing, the inflammation usually lasts for 2-5 DAYS`. **2-5 days runs INTO proliferation's 4-21.** Verified in the publisher's XML - both strings are in the same file, and the paper's own subject is the boundary between those two phases
span.quote: In normal skin wound healing, the inflammation usually lasts for 2–5 days and ceases once the harmful stimuli have been removed; even though the immune responses continue through the whole procedure of wound healing, evolving through progressive states of specific leukocyte involvement and function

span.label: the resolution half of the process is the unstudied half, and the review says so: `Compared with the process of initiation and amplification of the inflammatory response, WE KNOW MUCH LESS ABOUT HOW INFLAMMATION IS RESOLVED during normal wound healing, which is prerequisite for understanding the pathogenesis of persistent inflammation in chronic wounds`
span.quote: Compared with the process of initiation and amplification of the inflammatory response, we know much less about how inflammation is resolved during normal wound healing, which is prerequisite for understanding the pathogenesis of persistent inflammation in chronic wounds [ 6 ]. Moreover, the next step, proliferation, is tightly connected with the inflammatory response, and also plays an important role in resolving inflammation.

span.label: AND THE CANONICAL INDUCERS OF ONE OF THE TWO MACROPHAGE CLASSES TURN OUT NOT TO BE REQUIRED FOR IT: `IL-4 and IL-13 are THE CANONICAL FACTORS INDUCING THE M2 PHENOTYPE, however, recent studies show that THEY ARE NOT NECESSARY for modulating macrophage phenotypes in wounds in vivo`. The class survives the loss of its own definition
span.quote: As mentioned above, IL-4 and IL-13 are the canonical factors inducing the M2 phenotype, however, recent studies show that they are not necessary for modulating macrophage phenotypes in wounds in vivo

span.label: and the clinical problem the review is written for is stated as unsolved: `Chronic wounds are DIFFICULT TO TREAT due to their complex nature and OUR LIMITED UNDERSTANDING OF PATHOGENETIC MECHANISMS. Up to one-third of treated patients experience four or more episodes of recurrence`
span.quote: Chronic wounds are difficult to treat due to their complex nature and our limited understanding of pathogenetic mechanisms. Up to one-third of treated patients experience four or more episodes of recurrence [ 3 ]. Therefore, identification of new therapeutic targets is needed.

span.label: with the existing therapies described the same way: `Few targeted approaches have been developed to date, including mainly topical application of growth factors, UNFORTUNATELY WITH LIMITED CLINICAL EFFICACY`
span.quote: Current treatments for impaired wound healing focus mainly on optimisation of controllable healing factors, e.g., clearance of infection, mechanical protection and nutritional support. Few targeted approaches have been developed to date, including mainly topical application of growth factors, unfortunately with limited clinical efficacy [ 4 ]. Identification of new therapeutic targets and development of more effective treatments are needed.
